issues.failure_explanation: The functional F in the statement contains B(t), and u^* solves the equation with B(t). The proof drops B(t) entirely. It substitutes f = (i d_t - H)u^*, which holds only for B = 0, and concludes F(v) = ||u-u^*||_{X_H}^2. It then invokes the norm equivalence (i), which gives gamma = 1. For B != 0 the correct identity is F(v) = N(u-u^*)^2 with N from Theorem 3.1(ii), and only that part yields the (1+T)^{-2} lower bound. The proof also asserts ||u-u^*||_{X_{H_0}} = ||v-v^*||_{H^1(I,H)} without ever defining the H^1 norm. With the standard H^1 norm this identity is false, and the claimed T-independence of the constants is not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the proof with B(t) included, so that F(v) = N(u-u^*)^2 with f = (i d_t - H - B)u^*. Apply Theorem 3.1(ii) for B != 0 and (i) for B = 0. Fix the H^1 norm as |v(0)|^2 + T||v'||^2, or track the T-dependence of the norm conversion.
issues.overall_effect: The gamma = 2 (B != 0) part of the well-posedness estimate and the Cea-type bound with (1+T)^{gamma+1} are not established by the written proof. The statement itself is probably true via Theorem 3.1(ii).
issues.title: Proof of Corollary 3.1 ignores B(t) and so does not support the case gamma = 2
issues.why_classification: The needed ingredient (Theorem 3.1(ii)) already exists, so the repair is a short local rewrite that keeps the statement and rates.

issues.failure_explanation: Elements of Y_{H_0} must take values in D(H_0) with (i d_t - H_0)w in L^2. A function in C_c^infty(I, H) need not satisfy this, so the inclusion fails. The computation also uses (i d_t - H)e^{-itH}w with H in place of H_0, and it omits the term B(t) from S^*. Yet the proposition claims the equivalence for the full equation with A and B. As written, the converse (that S^*u = i delta_0 (x) u_0 + f implies that u is a weak solution of the full equation) is not proved.

failure_location.tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take test functions in C_c^infty(I, D(H_0)) and keep the B(t) term in the identity. Conclude that (i d_t - H - B)u = f weakly, then recover u(0) = u_0 from the boundary term as is done now.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if and only if' in part (i) is proved only in the forward direction. The converse is not used later, so Corollary L2 is unaffected.
issues.primary_affected_tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.title: Converse direction of Proposition S-star uses inadmissible test functions and drops A and B
issues.why_classification: The argument has the right structure and only the test class and the omitted bounded term need correcting. No result that is used later is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The inner integral over s in [0,t] is first enlarged to [0,T]. The next line then swaps the order of integration as if s <= t still held, giving int_s^infty e^{-mu t} dt = e^{-mu s}/mu. After the enlargement the correct expression is (int_0^T e^{-mu t} dt) * ||u-v||_{L^2}^2. This is not bounded by (1/mu) * int e^{-mu s}|u-v|^2, since the weight e^{-mu s} is missing and cannot be recovered without a factor e^{mu T}. So the step is invalid, and the claimed contraction constant M^2 T/mu is not obtained from this chain.

failure_location.quote: M^2 T \int_0^T \diff t \eexp^{-\mu t} \int_0^T \diff s \abs{u(s) - v(s)}^2

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the integral over s in [0,t] when applying Cauchy-Schwarz, use |int_0^t ...|^2 <= M^2 T int_0^t |u-v|^2, then swap integrals over s <= t. This gives int_s^T e^{-mu t} dt <= e^{-mu s}/mu and hence the contraction constant M^2 T/mu.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and uniqueness of the weak solution with B(t), and the continuity estimate that follows from it, rest on a flawed contraction estimate. The result itself is standard and true.
issues.title: Contraction estimate in the existence proof extends the time integral and breaks the exponential weight
issues.why_classification: A one-line standard weighted-norm argument fixes it and every claim and constant survives.
